title: Old vs New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC)
source: Income Tax Department, Government of India
content: The New Tax Regime under Section 115BAC is the default tax regime for individuals and HUFs. Under the New Tax Regime for Tax Year 2026-27, the 7-bracket income tax slab structure is: ₹0 to ₹4,00,000 (Nil), ₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 (5%), ₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 (10%), ₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 (15%), ₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 (20%), ₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 (25%), and Above ₹24,00,000 (30%). The New Regime offers lower tax slab rates but foregoes major Chapter VI-A deductions (80C, 80D, HRA). However, ₹75,000 Standard Deduction and employer NPS Section 80CCD(2) remain deductible under the New Regime. With the Section 87A rebate up to ₹60,000 for taxable income up to ₹12,00,000, taxpayers with ₹9 lakh income (or 9 lakh annual income) pay ₹0 tax under the New Regime. Under the Old Tax Regime, slab rates are higher (0-2.5L 0%, 2.5L-5L 5%, 5L-10L 20%, >10L 30%), but taxpayers can claim 80C, 80D, HRA, and home loan deductions.
